summary: The last 4 weeks show a very inconsistent training block with low overall volume across all three disciplines — only 9 sessions logged, dominated by short open-water swims and a single long ride. Recovery is severely compromised, with chronic sleep deprivation (multiple nights under 5 hours, including 41 min on July 27) and body battery readings frequently in the 2–25 range, indicating the athlete is carrying significant cumulative fatigue. With a sprint triathlon test race just 7 days away, the immediate priority must be rest and race-specific sharpening rather than any further load accumulation.
suggestions: Treat the next 7 days as a mini-taper: cap all sessions at 30–40 min of easy effort and prioritise 7–8 hours of sleep every night — your body battery data shows you are not currently absorbing any training stimulus meaningfully.

For the sprint test race (750m/20km/5km), do a short 10–15 min brick session on Saturday (Aug 1) — 10 min easy bike into 5 min easy run — just to rehearse the transitions and feel the bike-to-run change; this replaces the planned long ride.

Your swim pace in open water has been 24–28 min/km, which is significantly slower than the 1:50/100m Ironman target — prioritise pool sessions with drills over open-water social swims from Week 7 onward to build technique and efficiency.
The July 18 run at 179 bpm avg HR is a red flag for overreaching; enforce a strict HR ceiling of 145 bpm on all easy runs until sleep consistently averages 6.5+ hours per night.

From Week 9 onward, introduce structured 800m intervals for the Treviso 10K (64 days away) at 5:00–5:15/km as already planned — but only proceed if the preceding two long runs were completed without HR exceedances and sleep has stabilised.

proposed_changes.current_session: Long ride AI adjusted: 50–60km @ 128–145W, up to 150 min
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Replace with a 15–20 min easy brick: 10 min easy spin at 110–130W followed immediately by 5 min easy jog at 7:00/km — purely to rehearse the bike-to-run transition ahead of the test race on or around Aug 2.
proposed_changes.reason: With a sprint triathlon test race 7 days away and body battery critically low, a long aerobic ride adds fatigue with no fitness gain — a short brick is more race-specific and less costly.

proposed_changes.current_session: Long run AI adjusted: 7–8km @ 7:00/km, HR ≤145 bpm
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Skip or replace with a 20-min easy walk/jog if legs feel heavy — if the test race is on this day, this IS the race; do not double up with a training run.
proposed_changes.reason: If the test race falls on or near Aug 2, running a long session the same day defeats the purpose; if the race is later in the week, preserving freshness is more valuable than a short aerobic run.

proposed_changes.current_session: AI adjusted: 60 min Z2 at 128–155W, body battery gate of 40+
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Keep the 60 min Z2 ride at 128–145W only if body battery is 50+ after the test race weekend; if below 50, reduce to 30 min easy spin at 110–130W or skip entirely.
proposed_changes.reason: Post-race recovery is unpredictable and the body battery data shows the athlete is currently not bouncing back quickly between efforts.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: 70km @ 128–150W, strict 180-min ceiling, flat Malta roads; no tempo blocks — hold lower Z2 only and stop early if avg HR exceeds 138 bpm in the first 45 min.
proposed_changes.reason: The athlete's only long ride in 4 weeks was 77km with no power data; stepping to 84km+ in Week 7 is too aggressive given the ongoing sleep and recovery deficit.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: 3x800m @ 5:10–5:20/km with 2-min standing recovery, total 30–35 min including warm-up and cool-down — reduce rep count by one as this is the first structured interval block in the cycle.
proposed_changes.reason: The Treviso 10K is 64 days away and interval fitness must be built gradually; 3 reps at conservative pace reduces injury risk and allows the athlete to assess readiness before adding volume in Week 10.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: 16km @ 6:30–6:45/km (105 min), with the final 3km at 6:00–6:10/km only if HR has stayed under 145 bpm throughout — this adds a Treviso-pace touch without extending overall volume.
proposed_changes.reason: 18.5km is beyond what the athlete has demonstrated in recent weeks; capping at 16km with an optional race-pace finish builds Treviso 10K specificity without overreaching.
